lead.headline: Tether's KPMG Clean Opinion Marks First Full Audit Milestone as Hardware Wallet Security Model Fractures
lead.tldr: This week exposed a structural fault line in crypto's security stack: the same self-custody hardware vendors long marketed as 'unhackable' are now absorbing nine-figure losses, while institutional validation of onchain infrastructure—from Tether's audit to Franklin Templeton's SEC no-action letter—accelerates faster than retail risk tools can adapt.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the gap between institutional-grade onchain validation and retail self-custody security widened into a chasm worth tracking closely.

top_signals.title: Coldcard Exploit Abates as Total Losses Climb to (at Least) 1,700 BTC
top_signals.summary: A vulnerability in Coldcard hardware wallets has led to significant losses, with at least 1,700 BTC stolen. While new incidents of the exploit have slowed down, the total amount of lost funds continues to rise as more victims report their losses.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Coldcard exploit's climbing loss tally reframes hardware wallet security from a solved problem to an active underwriting concern for any fund with treasury exposure.

top_signals.title: Harmony confirms exploit involving unauthorized minting of 4 billion ONE tokens
top_signals.summary: Harmony has confirmed a security exploit involving the unauthorized minting of 4 billion ONE tokens. The breach was first reported by X user Juiceberg.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Harmony's unauthorized mint of 4 billion ONE tokens demonstrates that inflationary attack vectors remain unpriced in layer-1 governance and tokenomics models.

top_signals.title: Why the latest Bitcoin hack hurt more than most
top_signals.summary: A major security breach has resulted in the theft of $100 million from Coldcard hardware wallet users. The incident is particularly significant as it targeted users who followed strict security protocols.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $100 million Coldcard breach targeting users with strict security protocols destroys the retail assumption that operational discipline alone guarantees self-custody safety.

top_signals.title: Trump, CFTC Chair Selig expected at Wednesday White House meeting with crypto and prediction market executives
top_signals.summary: President Trump and CFTC Chair Rusty Selig are expected to meet with crypto and prediction market executives at the White House this Wednesday. The meeting serves as a kickoff for the CFTC's inaugural Innovation Advisory Committee meeting.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The White House-CFTC meeting with prediction market and crypto executives signals that regulated derivatives and event contracts are being fast-tracked as a bipartisan policy priority.

top_signals.title: Tether completes first full financial audit, receives clean KPMG opinion
top_signals.summary: Tether has completed its first full independent financial audit for its 2025 financial statements. The audit was conducted by KPMG, which issued a clean opinion on the stablecoin issuer's financials.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Tether's clean KPMG opinion removes the last credible objection to USDT's reserve backing for most institutional counterparties, repricing the stablecoin competitive landscape.

top_signals.title: SEC clears Franklin Templeton funds to use onchain BENJI system for cash management
top_signals.summary: The SEC has issued a no-action letter allowing Franklin Templeton's traditional registered funds to utilize its onchain BENJI system for cash management. This marks a significant step in integrating traditional finance (TradFi) with blockchain-based asset management.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The SEC's no-action letter for Franklin Templeton's onchain BENJI system creates a replicable template for TradFi funds seeking compliant tokenized cash management infrastructure.

deals.summary: Goldman Sachs is acquiring ETF manager NEOS Investments in a deal valued at up to $2.25 billion. This move integrates NEOS's Bitcoin and Ether-linked ETFs into Goldman's asset management division.

Nasdaq is acquiring LeveL Markets to advance its goal of creating 'always-on' financial markets. This move signals a shift toward 24/7 trading capabilities, mirroring the operational model of cryptocurrency markets.
eToro has reached an agreement to acquire TradeZero for a total value of up to $231 million. The move comes as eToro reports strong Q2 growth driven primarily by equities trading.

Galaxy has committed $50 million to USHP through a pre-launch institutional funding round. USHP is developing the first digital asset that references a U.S. home price index, bringing real estate pricing data onchain.
Mirae Asset plans to invest an additional $35 million into the Korbit crypto exchange. This follows the firm's acquisition of a 97.15% stake in the company in July for approximately $91.5 million.
H100 has significantly increased its Bitcoin holdings to 3,506 BTC through an acquisition deal. The transaction was funded by the issuance of 790.5 million new shares.

Sweden-based company H100 has significantly increased its Bitcoin holdings to 3,506 BTC following a recent acquisition of 2,455 BTC. This move establishes H100 as the second-largest Bitcoin treasury in Europe.

on_the_radar.title: Bank of England tests stablecoin, digital pound interoperability in cross-border payments34m
on_the_radar.summary: The Bank of England is conducting tests to ensure interoperability between a potential digital pound (CBDC) and private stablecoins for cross-border payments. This initiative aims to modernize the UK's payment infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of international settlements.

on_the_radar.title: Wintermute to pour $1B into AI, high-frequency trading amid TradFi expansion: Report28m
on_the_radar.summary: Wintermute plans to invest $1 billion into AI and high-frequency trading as part of its expansion into traditional finance (TradFi). The move signals a strategic push to integrate advanced trading technologies across both crypto and conventional markets.

on_the_radar.title: Fidelity files with SEC to add staking to Ethereum ETF16m, Fidelity files with SEC to add staking to Ethereum ETFFidelity plans to add staking to its Ether fund, with 85% of rewards retained by FETH and quarterly cash distributions planned for investors.
on_the_radar.summary: Fidelity has filed with the SEC to incorporate staking rewards into its Ethereum ETF. The proposal suggests that 85% of rewards would be retained by the fund, with quarterly cash distributions provided to investors.

on_the_radar.title: SEC, CFTC sue Goliath Ventures over $400M crypto Ponzi scheme
on_the_radar.summary: The SEC and CFTC have filed lawsuits against Goliath Ventures in connection with a $400 million cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme. While Delgado has agreed to settle with the SEC, the CFTC is pursuing further penalties and market bans.

on_the_radar.title: SEC could propose 'pivotal' crypto rules that may start with token safe harbor, TD Cowen says
on_the_radar.summary: TD Cowen suggests that an upcoming SEC meeting could initiate a pivotal rulemaking process for crypto. This may include the introduction of a token safe harbor, potentially providing much-needed regulatory clarity for the industry.

on_the_radar.title: Robinhood Vault: Retail Lenders, Institutional Borrowers
on_the_radar.summary: Robinhood has launched a curated Morpho vault for USDG, rapidly scaling to $600M in TVL and $287M in loans within one month. The vault allows Robinhood's retail user base to earn a 7% APY by providing liquidity to institutional borrowers.

on_the_radar.title: Russia proposes exchange trading of Bitcoin, Ether and Tether’s USDT
on_the_radar.summary: The Bank of Russia has proposed allowing the trading of Bitcoin, Ether, and USDT on regulated exchanges. The central bank is currently seeking public feedback on this proposal until August 24.

on_the_radar.title: Anthropic strikes $9B compute deal with Bitcoin miner Riot: Report21m, Anthropic strikes $9B compute deal with Bitcoin miner Riot: ReportAnthropic reportedly struck a $9 billion deal with Riot for 191 megawatts of capacity from the Bitcoin miner’s Rockdale campus in Texas.
on_the_radar.summary: AI firm Anthropic has reportedly entered into a $9 billion agreement with Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms to utilize compute capacity. The deal involves 191 megawatts of power from Riot's Rockdale campus in Texas.

on_the_radar.title: Broadridge's Distributed Ledger Repo platform processes $8 trillion in July volume
on_the_radar.summary: Broadridge's distributed ledger-based repo platform achieved a massive milestone by processing $8 trillion in volume during July. This demonstrates significant institutional adoption of blockchain technology for traditional financial settlement.

on_the_radar.title: Wallet provider SafePal says data breach exposed personal info of nearly 40,000 customers
on_the_radar.summary: Wallet provider SafePal has confirmed a data breach that exposed the personal information of approximately 40,000 customers. While the company recently identified the root cause, users had reported phishing attempts linked to the breach as early as July.

on_the_radar.title: ‘The great quantum migration’ is coming as more than $2 trillion in digital assets is at risk—nearly the entire value of the overall crypto market
on_the_radar.summary: The crypto market faces a systemic risk as quantum computing threatens the elliptic-curve cryptography securing over $2 trillion in digital assets. Quantus CEO Christoper Smith warns of a necessary 'great quantum migration' to protect the industry from future quantum attacks.

on_the_radar.title: Israel’s largest bank taps Galaxy to offer bitcoin, ether and solana trading
on_the_radar.summary: Israel's largest bank is partnering with Galaxy to provide trading services for Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana. This move follows data showing significant on-chain crypto value flowing into Israel.

worth_a_read.title: Committing $50M to USHP: The Product Bringing U.S. Home Prices Onchain
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's $50M commitment to USHP offers a concrete look at how institutional capital is underwriting real estate index tokenization and the oracle mechanics required to make it work.

worth_a_read.title: Weekly Research Brief: SEC Scrambles to Act as CLARITY Fizzles
worth_a_read.note: The Galaxy brief on SEC scrambling post-CLARITY fizzle tracks how regulatory vacuum is being filled by agency enforcement rather than legislation, with direct implications for portfolio construction timelines.

worth_a_read.title: State of TRON Q2 2026
worth_a_read.note: Messari's TRON Q2 analysis provides the data to test whether USDT supply concentration on the network is stabilizing or accelerating, which matters for Tether's newly audited liability structure.

worth_a_read.title: The Case For Plasma One: Stablecoins Are Eating The World
worth_a_read.note: Delphi's Plasma One case reframes stablecoin growth not as payment rail adoption but as sovereign debt market displacement, a thesis worth stress-testing against Tether's audit disclosure.

worth_a_read.title: Solana Q2 2026 Update: Building for the Tokenized Economy
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's Solana Q2 update maps the protocol's institutional infrastructure buildout against Franklin Templeton's BENJI approval, showing where tokenized economy tooling is actually shipping versus pitched.

linkedin_post:
Tether just got a clean opinion from KPMG on its first full audit. That sentence would have been unthinkable three years ago. We underwrote stablecoin risk on reserve opacity; that variable is now being priced out for USDT specifically, which reprices every competitor against a verified liability stack.

The same week, Coldcard users who followed every operational security protocol lost $100 million to a hardware exploit. The self-custody hardware sector is not being underwritten for firmware supply chain risk, and the loss curve is still climbing past 1,700 BTC.

These two signals do not balance. They split the market into institutional infrastructure that can pass Big Four audit and retail security tools that cannot survive targeted exploitation. Franklin Templeton's SEC no-action letter for onchain BENJI cash management is the logical next step: regulated funds will use tokenized rails, but they will not use them through hardware wallets.

The testable thesis: if Tether's audit triggers a wave of corporate treasury adoption, the stablecoin market bifurcates between audited and unaudued issuers by Q1. If Coldcard-class exploits repeat, hardware wallet market share shifts to custodial or multi-sig alternatives regardless of Bitcoin maximalist preference. One of these is already happening. The other depends on whether vendors treat firmware as a security surface or a marketing afterthought.

We are watching which stablecoin competitor publishes audit dates next, and which hardware vendor publishes a credible root cause on the Coldcard exploit. Neither has yet.
